Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shafaq Fatima Hon'ble Pankaj Bhatia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Ms. Mansi Gupta, Advocate appearing on behalf of Ms.
Shafaq Fatima, learned counsel for the respondent complainant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2.
In terms of the F.I.R. lodged by the informant it was alleged that the applicant was forming physical relations with the victim for the last six years on the false pretext of marriage.
It was also stated that during the said period, physical relations were formed at various occasions.

3. In the light of the said, counsel for the applicant places reliance on the judgements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Deepak Gulati Vs. State of Haryana : AIR 2013 SC 2071 to argue that admittedly physical relations continued in between the parties for a span of six years, as such no Arshad vs State Of U.P Thru. Secy. Home Deptt. ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41257891/
1 case can be said to be made out against the applicant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Arshad vs State Of U.P Thru. Secy. Home Deptt
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The applicant is in custody since 20.3.2024 having no criminal antecedents, hence the applicant may be released on bail.
4. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail.

5. What transpires from the record that this court had granted an interim bail to the accused applicant vide order dated 16.5.2024 recording the undertaking given on behalf of the applicant that the applicant is ready and willing to marry the victim.

However, on 30.7.2024, the applicant was present and specifically stated that he is not ready to marry the victim, as such the interim bail granted to the applicant was cancelled and the matter was directed to be heard on merits on today i.e. 13.8.2024.
6.
Today the matter is heard on merits.

7. Considering the F.I.R. and the allegations made therein that the applicant and the victim stayed together for almost six years and physical relations continued in between them over a long period on the false pretext of marriage and considering the age of the victim to be around 22 years and keeping in view the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Deepak Gulati Vs. State of Haryana : AIR 2013 SC 2071, and the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is languishing in jail since 20.3.2024 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
8.

entities.text: Deepak Gulati Vs. State of Haryana : AIR 2013 SC 2071
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

9. Let the applicant Arshad be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.128 of 2024, under Sections 376, 504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 67 of the Information Technology Act, Police Station Safdarganj,
District Barabanki on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
